sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed by the appellants/ claimants challenging the judgment and decree passed in M.C.O.P.No.7116 of 2015 dated 12.10.2020 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Principal Special Judge, Special Court under E.C. & NDPS Act, Chennai  104.
2.The

learned counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that on 24.07.2015 at about 12.15 p.m., the deceased Selvakumar was riding the motor cycle bearing Registration No.TN 18 F 8215 towards Manali Pudhu Nagar to Ponneri High Road.

At that time, the driver of the bus bearing Registration No.TN 01 N 9776 belonging to the respondent drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle, due to which, the deceased lost his life.

3.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants further submitted that thereafter, the wife, son and parents of the deceased Selvakumar/ appellants/ claimants filed claim petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, claiming a sum of Rs.50 Lakhs as compensation.

After adjudication, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.38,28,000/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the petition i.e.,
10.09.2015 till the date of realization with proportionate costs and directed the respondent to deposit the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement in compensation.

4.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants further submitted that the deceased was working as an Executive in German Express Shipping Agency, Kondakarai and was earning a sum of Rs.32,000/- per month and to prove the same, the claimants marked Ex.P9  salary proof before the Tribunal, however, the Tribunal without considering the same, fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month and awarded a meagre compensation and hence, the appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation.

5.Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent Transport Corporation submitted that though the claimants marked Ex.P9  salary proof before the Tribunal, in the absence of oral evidence by the employer or author of the salary proof, the salary proof marked by the claimants is not admissible.

In the present case, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis there are contrary statement available in the claim petition and before the Tribunal and hence, the Tribunal fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month and further submitted that the Tribunal after considering all the factual aspects, awarded the compensation which is just and reasonable and hence, the impugned judgment warrants no interference.
6.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants as well as the learned counsel appearing for the respondent and perused the materials available on record.

8.The tribunal after elaborately discussing the factual aspects awarded a sum of Rs.32,13,000/- for loss of dependency, Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses, Rs.2,00,000/- for loss of consortium to the f i r s t a p p e l l a n t , R s . 2 , 0 0 , 0 0 0 / - f o r l o s s o f l o v e a n d a f f e c t i o n t o t h e s e c o n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis appellant, Rs.2,00,000/- for loss of love and affection to the appellants 3 and 4 (Rs.1,00,000/- each) and arrived at a total compensation of Rs.38,28,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition i.e., 10.09.2015 till the date of realization.

9.In the claim petition, the claimants claim that the deceased earned Rs.20,000/- per month and Ex.P9  salary proof marked by the claimants before the Tribunal shows that the deceased earned a sum of Rs.32,000/- per month and both the claims are not supported by any oral evidence

and hence the Tribunal applied the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma and Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in 2009 (2) L.S. 29 (S.C.) and fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month and awarded compensation, which is perfectly in order.

Further, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- for loss of consortium to the first appellant, Rs.2,00,000/- for loss of love and affection to the second appellant,
Rs.2,00,000/- for loss of love and affection to the appellants 3 and 4 (Rs.1,00,000/- each), even then the appellants have filed this appeal for enhancement of compensation, which is not sustainable one.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis M.DHANDAPANI,J.
pri 10.The civil miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
